item.title: A Neural Network That Computes With Light in a Fiber
item.description: Researchers at the University of Tokyo and NTT built a neural network around a single loop of optical fiber. Light pulses circling the loop do the computing. Their new training method, state-skipping direct feedback alignment, learns from the final error and never needs to read the loop's hidden states. On the real optoelectronic setup it reached about 97% accuracy on handwritten digits (MNIST). I

item.title: How an Octopus Pours Itself Through a Tiny Hole
item.description: How does a soft animal with eight arms get its whole body through a hole narrower than the gap between its eyes? Researchers filmed three common octopuses crossing a clear partition 30 times. Every pass followed the same order: probe with one arm, push 3–5 arms through, then anchor and pull.
